entities.summary:
Gojslav of Croatia was a monarch who co-ruled the Kingdom of Croatia with his brother Krešimir III from 1000 to his death in 1020. He was the youngest son of the former Croatian King Stjepan Držislav and a member of the royal House of Trpimirović. 

Born around 980, Gojslav ascended to the throne after his brother Krešimir III's marriage to his first cousin, a practice known as endogamy. This union strengthened the ties between the Croatian royal family and the powerful Pannonian nobility. 

During his reign, Gojslav oversaw the construction of several churches, including the magnificent cathedral at Zadar, which became a model for future Byzantine architecture. He also encouraged trade and commerce, establishing the city of Zadar as a major center of maritime trade. 

Gojslav's legacy extends beyond the Kingdom of Croatia, as his diplomatic and military efforts helped to secure the borders of the Eastern Roman Empire. He played a key role in the Byzantine-Croatian alliance, which would prove crucial in the face of future threats from the Hungarians and the Pannonians. 

In his later years, Gojslav became increasingly concerned about the threat of the Hungarians, who had begun to encroach on Croatian territory. He took steps to strengthen the kingdom's defenses, including the construction of new fortifications and the recruitment of mercenary forces. 

Despite his efforts, Gojslav was ultimately unable to stem the tide of Hungarian expansion, and he died in 1020, bringing an end to his reign and the beginning of a new era for the Kingdom of Croatia.
